newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Tuesday on long liquidation from retail investors, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at 3,320 yuan ($400) per tonne, losing four yuan. It opened at 3,320 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 3,330 and a low of 3,318.
March rose 81 yuan to 3,211, May did not trade, July fell 25 to 3,330, November four to 3,330 and the January 1998 contract three to 3,340.
Combined volume fell to 22,700 tonnnes from 23,800.
Traders said retail investors dominated today's trading with many institutional investors remaining on the sidelines.

"Active stock markets and other futures markets attracted capital from the soybean market," one trader said. "The general outlook is not very optimistic but sharp falls are impossible with less and less investors trading on the market."
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around the current level in the next few days.
